mainTopic: קרח's rebellion: the two wives, the seriousness of מחלוקת and opposing one's רבי, קרח's wealth and death, and the fate of his group
overview: This amud opens at the end of the story of און בן פלת's wife, whose clever trick kept her husband away from קרח's group. The גמרא then tells how קרח's wife pushed him into the rebellion with complaints against משה, and reads משלי 14:1 about the two wives. Next it explains who the 250 men with קרח were, and what slander made משה fall on his face. From משה going to דתן ואבירם, the גמרא learns that keeping a מחלוקת going is forbidden. It then teaches that fighting with, complaining about, or even suspecting one's רבי is like doing so against the שכינה. The גמרא describes קרח's huge wealth, which came from יוסף's hidden treasure, and brings two views on whether קרח was swallowed, burned, or neither. It ends with aggadot: the sun and moon protesting for משה, משה asking for the opening of גיהנם to be brought close, the sons of קרח singing in a safe spot, and the swallowed group admitting that משה and his תורה are true.

steps.title: און בן פלת's wife keeps the rebels away and he is saved
steps.stepSummary: On בן פלת's wife uncovered her hair at the tent entrance. Everyone who came to call On turned back, and meanwhile קרח's group was swallowed up.
steps.simpleTranslation: And she uncovered her hair. Anyone who came and saw her turned back. In the meantime, they (קרח's group) were swallowed into the ground.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the story of how On בן פלת's wife saved her husband from being swallowed with קרח's group.
steps.deeperAnalysis: She sat at the tent entrance with her hair uncovered. The rebels were modest people who would not look at a woman like that, so they stepped back and did not come in to call On. By the time the danger passed, קרח's group had already been swallowed, and On stayed safe at home.

phrases.english: and she uncovered her hair,
phrases.notes: "She" is און בן פלת's wife, sitting at the tent's entrance.

phrases.english: anyone who came and saw her turned back.
In the meantime, they were swallowed up.
phrases.notes: "They" means קרח and his group.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the On בן פלת story, which began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On's wife's clever, modest-minded trick kept the rebels away until קרח's group was swallowed, so On was saved.

steps.title: קרח's wife complains that משה grabbed all the honor
steps.stepSummary: קרח's wife tells him that משה made himself king and his family כהנים. She says he takes gifts away from the לויים and humiliates them by shaving and waving them.
steps.simpleTranslation: קרח's wife said to him: Look what משה is doing! He became king. He made his brother כהן גדול and his brother's sons deputy כהנים. When תרומה comes, he says it goes to the כהן. When מעשר comes, which you לויים take, he says: give one tenth to the כהן. And besides that, he shaves off your hair and waves you around like dung, as if he had his eye on your hair.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now tells the opposite story: how קרח's wife pushed her husband into the rebellion. She does this by painting משה as power-hungry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: She lists three complaints. First, משה kept the top positions in his own family. Second, even the gifts the לויים receive get a cut taken for the כהנים. Third, the shaving and waving of the לויים (במדבר 8) was really meant to make them look ugly and lowly. Her goal is to make קרח feel cheated and insulted.

keyTerms.meaning: Deputy כהנים, assistants of the כהן גדול
The portion of produce given to the כהן
The tenth of produce given to the לוי
Waves (from תנופה, the waving done to the לויים)

phrases.english: Korach's wife said to him:
See what Moses is doing.
He became the king,
he made his brother High Priest,
he made his brother's sons deputy priests.
If terumah comes, he says: "Let it be for the priest,"
if the tithe comes, which you take,
phrases.notes: "You" means the לויים, who receive the first מעשר.

phrases.english: he says: "Give one out of ten to the priest."
And furthermore, he shears off your hair
and waves you around like dung,
phrases.notes: במדבר 8:5–11

phrases.english: he set his eye on your hair.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts the wise wife (On's) with the foolish one (קרח's).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קרח's wife accuses משה of grabbing power for his family and degrading the לויים.

steps.title: קרח objects that משה shaved too, and his wife answers
steps.stepSummary: קרח points out that משה also shaved like the other לויים. His wife answers that משה was willing to humiliate himself just to humiliate them.
steps.simpleTranslation: קרח said to her: But he did the same thing himself! She said to him: Since everything is for his own greatness, he also said, "Let me die with the Philistines."
steps.whatsHappening: קרח pushes back on his wife's claim, and she brushes his objection aside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קרח's point: if משה shaved himself too, the shaving can't be a plot to shame the לויים. She answers with שמשון's words from שופטים: someone set on bringing others down will gladly suffer the same thing himself. In her eyes, משה shaved too just so he could shame everyone else.

keyTerms.meaning: "Let me die with the Philistines" (שמשון's words)

phrases.english: He said to her:
But he too did it!
phrases.notes: משה was also a לוי, so he was shaved along with them.

phrases.english: She said to him:
Since all of it is for his own greatness,
he too said
"Let me die with the Philistines."
phrases.notes: שופטים 16:30. She means: he'll hurt himself if it brings you down too.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the shaving complaint from step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The wife's claim that the shaving was meant to shame the לויים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: משה shaved himself as well, so it can't be a plan aimed against them.
steps.terutzMaskana: He was willing to suffer the shame himself in order to shame everyone else, like שמשון.

steps.title: קרח's wife mocks the מצוה of תכלת
steps.stepSummary: She adds another complaint: if תכלת is so important, משה should just dress his whole yeshiva in all-תכלת cloaks.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, about what he told you, to make תכלת: if you think תכלת counts as a מצוה, then bring out cloaks made of תכלת and cover your entire yeshiva with them!
steps.whatsHappening: קרח's wife adds a further argument: that משה's command about תכלת is made up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: She takes a mocking stance. If one thread of תכלת is a מצוה, then a whole garment of תכלת should be even better, without any ציצית. Since משה doesn't say that, she suggests he is simply inventing rules.

keyTerms.meaning: תכלת, the sky-blue dye used for ציצית
If it enters your mind, if you think

phrases.english: And furthermore, that which he told you: make sky-blue dye.
If it enters your mind
phrases.notes: She switches to talking as if she were answering משה directly.

phrases.english: that sky-blue dye is considered [a מצוה],
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in square brackets and some don't.

phrases.english: take out cloaks of sky-blue dye
and cover your entire academy with them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a further complaint to her list from step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: She mocks תכלת to show that משה invents laws on his own.

steps.title: The פסוק about the wise woman and the foolish woman
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא connects the two wives to משלי 14:1. On's wife is the wise woman who builds her house, and קרח's wife is the foolish one who tears it down.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what is written: "The wisdom of women builds her house." This is the wife of On בן פלת. "And folly tears it down with her hands." This is the wife of קרח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wraps up both wife stories by reading a פסוק in משלי about them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first half of the פסוק fits On's wife, who saved her family. The second half fits קרח's wife, whose words destroyed hers. This shows how much a wife's advice can decide a family's fate.
steps.whatToRemember: On's wife saved her husband with wisdom. קרח's wife destroyed hers with complaints. משלי 14:1 describes them both.

phrases.english: This is what is written:
"The wisdom of women builds her house"
phrases.notes: משלי 14:1

phrases.aramaic: זוֹ אִשְׁתּוֹ שֶׁל אוֹן בֶּן פֶּלֶת,
phrases.english: this is the wife of On, son of Peleth,
"and folly tears it down with her hands"
this is the wife of Korach.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sums up both wife stories with a פסוק.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A wise wife builds her home, as On's wife did. A foolish wife destroys it, as קרח's wife did.

steps.title: Who the 250 men with קרח were
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the words of במדבר 16:2. The 250 men were the distinguished ones of the nation, experts in setting the calendar, and famous all over the world.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And they rose up before משה, with men from בני ישראל, 250 princes of the congregation": these were the special people of the community. "Called to the appointed time": they knew how to make leap years and set the months. "Men of name": they had a reputation throughout the whole world.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the פסוקים of the קרח story and explains, phrase by phrase, who the 250 men were.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each phrase of the פסוק is read as praise. "קריאי מועד" is linked to the word מועד (festival time), so these men knew how to set the calendar. "אנשי שם" means they were world-famous. The point is that קרח's followers were great people, not just a mob.

keyTerms.meaning: Those called to the appointed time
To make leap years (add a month)
To set when each month begins

phrases.english: "And they rose up before Moses
phrases.notes: במדבר 16:2

phrases.english: and men from the children of Israel
two hundred and fifty [princes of the congregation]"
phrases.notes: Some versions add the words in square brackets. They're the part of the פסוק explained right after.

phrases.english: the distinguished ones of the congregation,
"called to the appointed time"
who knew how to make leap years
and set the months,
"men of name"
who had a name throughout the whole world.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַיָּקֻמוּ לִפְנֵי מֹשֶׁה וַאֲנָשִׁים מִבְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the wife stories back to explaining the פסוקים of the rebellion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 250 men were the community's elite: calendar experts with a worldwide reputation.

steps.title: What did משה hear that made him fall on his face?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the פסוק that משה heard something and fell on his face, and asks what that report was.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And משה heard and he fell on his face." What report did he hear?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new פסוק about קרח and asks what exactly משה heard. This step sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says משה 'heard' something but never says what. Falling on his face shows it hurt him deeply, so the גמרא wants to know what the report was.

keyTerms.meaning: And he fell on his face

phrases.english: "And Moshe heard and he fell on his face."
phrases.notes: במדבר 16:4

phrases.english: What report did he hear?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from describing the 250 men to the next פסוק in the קרח story.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What report caused משה to fall on his face?

steps.title: They suspected משה of being with married women
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר נחמני in the name of רבי יונתן says that people suspected משה of sinning with married women, based on a פסוק in תהלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר נחמני said in the name of רבי יונתן: they suspected him of being with a married woman, as it says, "And they were jealous of משה in the camp."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: משה heard that people suspected him of being with married women.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof is the word וַיְקַנְאוּ in תהלים, which the גמרא reads as the kind of jealousy a husband feels about his wife. That is a hurtful accusation, and it explains why משה fell on his face.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said
in the name of Rabbi Yonatan:
That they suspected him with a married woman,
as it says: "And they were jealous of Moshe in the camp."
phrases.notes: תהלים 106:16

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן שֶׁחֲשָׁדוּהוּ מֵאֵשֶׁת אִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: משה heard that people suspected him of being with married women.

steps.title: Every man warned his wife to keep away from משה
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר יצחק adds that every man warned his wife not to be alone with משה, which is why משה moved his tent outside the camp.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר יצחק said: This teaches that each and every man warned his wife about משה, as it says, "And משה would take the tent and pitch it outside the camp."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמואל בר יצחק adds more detail to the suspicion: every husband warned his wife to keep away from משה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He brings a second פסוק to show how far the suspicion went. משה moving his tent out of the camp is read as his reaction to this slander.

keyTerms.meaning: Warned (a husband warning his wife not to be alone with a certain man)

phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Yitzchak said:
This teaches that each and every man
warned his wife about Moshe,
phrases.notes: He means each husband told his wife not to be alone with משה.

phrases.english: as it says: "And Moshe would take the tent
and pitch it outside the camp."
phrases.notes: שמות 33:7

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר יִצְחָק מְלַמֵּד שֶׁכׇּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד קִנֵּא אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ מִמֹּשֶׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 8 by describing how far the suspicion against משה went.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every man warned his wife to keep away from משה, so משה moved his tent outside the camp.

steps.title: משה went to דתן ואבירם: we may not keep a fight going
steps.stepSummary: From the פסוק that משה got up and went to דתן ואבירם, ריש לקיש learns that one may not keep a מחלוקת going.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And משה rose and went to דתן ואבירם." ריש לקיש said: From here we learn that one may not keep a dispute going.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new פסוק and ריש לקיש learns a lesson from it: we must not keep a fight alive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דתן ואבירם were the ones who attacked משה, yet משה himself went to them to try to make peace. If even the hurt side must try to end the fight, then nobody may hold on to a מחלוקת.

keyTerms.meaning: Keeping a dispute going, holding on to a fight

phrases.english: "And Moshe rose and went to Datan and Aviram."
phrases.notes: במדבר 16:25

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
From here we learn that one may not keep a dispute going,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ מִכָּאן שֶׁאֵין מַחְזִיקִין בְּמַחְלוֹקֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new פסוק in the קרח story and draws a practical lesson from it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may not keep a מחלוקת going; even the wronged side should try to end it.

steps.title: רב: keeping a fight going breaks a לאו
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports ריש לקיש with רב's teaching that anyone who keeps a fight going breaks a לאו, learned from the פסוק 'ולא יהיה כקרח וכעדתו'.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב said: Anyone who keeps a dispute going breaks a לאו, as it says, "And he will not be like קרח and his group."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רב's teaching to show that ריש לקיש's lesson is a real איסור, not just good advice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש learned from משה's actions that one should not keep a fight going. רב adds that this is an actual לאו, learned from the פסוק warning people not to be like קרח and his group.
steps.whyThisMatters: This turns the קרח story into a lasting halacha: keeping a fight going is forbidden by a לאו in the תורה.

phrases.english: As Rav said:
Anyone who keeps a dispute going breaks a negative commandment,
as it says: "And he will not be like Korach and his group."
phrases.notes: במדבר 17:5

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַב כׇּל הַמַּחְזִיק בְּמַחְלוֹקֶת עוֹבֵר בְּלָאו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for ריש לקיש's rule in step 10.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that one may not keep a מחלוקת going.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב's teaching based on 'ולא יהיה כקרח וכעדתו' (במדבר 17:5).

steps.title: רב אשי: one who keeps a fight going deserves צרעת
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says someone who keeps a fight going deserves צרעת, learning it from the shared word 'לו' in the קרח פסוק and in the פסוק where משה's hand became leprous.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: He deserves to be struck with צרעת. It is written here, "by the hand of משה to him," and it is written there, "And ה' said further to him: put your hand into your bosom."
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי adds what punishment fits someone who keeps a fight going: he deserves צרעת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about קרח ends with 'בְּיַד מֹשֶׁה לוֹ'. The words 'hand' and 'to him' also show up when ה' told משה to put his hand in his bosom and it came out with צרעת. That link teaches that the fitting punishment is צרעת.

keyTerms.meaning: It is written here... and it is written there (linking two פסוקים by a shared word)
Your bosom, the fold of your garment

steps.confusionAlert: רב אשי is not giving a new topic. He is still talking about the person who keeps a fight going from step 11, and the פסוק 'ביד משה לו' is the end of the same פסוק רב quoted.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
"He deserves to be struck with tzaraat."
It is written here: "by the hand of Moshe to him,"
phrases.notes: This is the end of the same פסוק, במדבר 17:5.

phrases.english: and it is written there:
"And ה׳ said further to him:
put now your hand into your bosom."
phrases.notes: שמות 4:6. There, משה's hand came out white with צרעת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the punishment for the איסור that רב taught in step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who keeps a מחלוקת going deserves צרעת, learned from the shared words 'יד' and 'לו'.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: challenging מלכות בית דוד deserves a snake bite
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי teaches that anyone who challenges the kingship of בית דוד deserves to be bitten by a snake, linking אדוניהו's 'אבן הזוחלת' to 'זוחלי עפר' in the תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said: Anyone who challenges the kingship of בית דוד deserves to be bitten by a snake. It is written here, "And אדוניהו slaughtered sheep and cattle and fatlings by the stone of זוחלת," and it is written there, "with the poison of crawling things of the dust."
steps.whatsHappening: Still on the topic of fighting against rightful leadership, רבי יוסי says that anyone who challenges מלכות בית דוד deserves a snake bite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אדוניהו tried to take the kingship while דוד was alive, and he held his feast by 'אבן הזוחלת'. The word זוחל also appears in the תורה for crawling, poisonous snakes, so the fitting punishment is a snake bite.

keyTerms.meaning: The kingship of the house of דוד
For a snake to bite him
Son of דוד who tried to take the throne

steps.whatToRemember: Fighting against rightful leadership is very serious: keeping a מחלוקת going breaks a לאו and deserves צרעת, and challenging מלכות בית דוד deserves a snake bite.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei said:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הַחוֹלֵק עַל מַלְכוּת בֵּית דָּוִד
phrases.english: Anyone who challenges the kingship of the house of David
deserves to be bitten by a snake.
It is written here: "And Adoniyahu slaughtered sheep and cattle
phrases.notes: מלכים א 1:9

phrases.english: and fatlings by the stone of Zochelet,"
and it is written there: "with the poison of crawling things of the dust."
phrases.notes: דברים 32:24. The shared word is זוחל, crawling, which describes snakes.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי כׇּל הַחוֹלֵק עַל מַלְכוּת בֵּית דָּוִד רָאוּי לְהַכִּישׁוֹ נָחָשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of punishments for fighting against rightful leadership, now applied to מלכות בית דוד.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who challenges מלכות בית דוד deserves to be bitten by a snake, learned from the shared word זוחל.

steps.title: Disagreeing with your teacher is like disagreeing with the Divine Presence
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא teaches that whoever disagrees with his רבי is like someone who disagrees with the שכינה, learned from the פסוק about דתן ואבירם.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: Anyone who disagrees with his teacher is like someone who disagrees with the Divine Presence, as it says: "When they fought against ה׳."
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא gives a new teaching. Fighting against your רבי counts as fighting against the שכינה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק is about דתן ואבירם, who really argued with משה. Yet the תורה says they fought "against ה׳." So opposing one's teacher is treated as opposing ה׳ Himself.

keyTerms.meaning: Disagrees with or opposes his teacher

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
Anyone who disagrees with his teacher
is like one who disagrees with the Divine Presence,
as it says: "When they fought against ה׳."
phrases.notes: במדבר 26:9. It is about דתן ואבירם, whose fight was really with משה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: כׇּל הַחוֹלֵק עַל רַבּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the punishments for a מחלוקת to a new series about honoring one's רבי, still built on the קרח story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Disagreeing with one's רבי is like disagreeing with the שכינה.

steps.title: Quarreling with your teacher is like quarreling with the Divine Presence
steps.stepSummary: רבי חמא ברבי חנינא teaches that starting a quarrel with one's רבי is like quarreling with the שכינה, learned from מי מריבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חמא ברבי חנינא said: Anyone who starts a quarrel with his teacher is like someone who quarrels with the Divine Presence, as it says: "These are the waters of quarrel, where בני ישראל quarreled with ה׳."
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא adds a similar teaching. This one is about starting an open quarrel with one's רבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At מי מריבה the people argued with משה about water. The פסוק still says they quarreled "with ה׳." So a quarrel with a teacher is counted as a quarrel with the שכינה.

keyTerms.meaning: The "waters of quarrel," where the people fought with משה over water

phrases.english: Rabbi Chama son of Rabbi Chanina said:
Anyone who makes a quarrel with his teacher
is like one who makes it with the Divine Presence,
as it says: "These are the waters of quarrel

phrases.aramaic: אֲשֶׁר רָבוּ בְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶת ה׳״.
phrases.english: where the Children of Israel quarreled with ה׳."
phrases.notes: במדבר 20:13

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חָמָא בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא: כָּל הָעוֹשֶׂה מְרִיבָה עִם רַבּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, parallel teaching about a different kind of wrong against one's רבי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Quarreling with one's רבי is like quarreling with the שכינה.

steps.title: Complaining about your teacher is like complaining about the Divine Presence
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא בר פפא teaches that complaining against one's רבי is like complaining against the שכינה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא בר פפא said: Anyone who complains against his teacher is as if he complains against the Divine Presence, as it says: "Your complaints are not against us, but against ה׳."
steps.whatsHappening: A third אמורא continues the series. This time the wrong is grumbling or complaining about one's רבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here משה himself, speaking for himself and אהרן, tells the people that their complaints are really against ה׳. This teaches that grumbling against a teacher is grumbling against the שכינה, even without an open fight.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina bar Pappa said:
Anyone who complains against his teacher
it is as if he complains against the Divine Presence,
as it says: "Your complaints are not against us
but against ה׳."
phrases.notes: שמות 16:8. משה is the one speaking here.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בַּר פָּפָּא: כׇּל הַמִּתְרַעֵם עַל רַבּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third parallel teaching, moving from open quarrels to complaining.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Complaining against one's רבי is like complaining against the שכינה.

steps.title: Suspecting your teacher is like suspecting the Divine Presence
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו teaches that even thinking bad thoughts or suspicions about one's רבי is like doing so about the שכינה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: Anyone who has suspicious thoughts about his teacher is as if he has suspicious thoughts about the Divine Presence, as it says: "And the people spoke against God and against משה."
steps.whatsHappening: A fourth אמורא ends the series. He says that even doubting or suspecting one's רבי counts as doing so about the שכינה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק puts God and משה side by side in the same sentence. That shows they are treated alike here. This is the lightest wrong in the list, only in the mind, and it is still treated as against the שכינה.

keyTerms.meaning: Has doubts or suspicious thoughts about someone

steps.whatToRemember: Four אמוראים, four levels: disagreeing, quarreling, complaining, and even suspecting your רבי. All of them are treated as being against the שכינה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abahu said:
Anyone who has suspicious thoughts about his teacher
it is as if he has suspicious thoughts about the Divine Presence,
as it says: "And the people spoke against God and against Moshe."
phrases.notes: במדבר 21:5

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ: כׇּל הַמְהַרְהֵר אַחַר רַבּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The fourth and final teaching in the series about one's רבי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Suspecting one's רבי is like suspecting the שכינה.

steps.title: Wealth that harms its owner is קרח's wealth
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש explains that the פסוק about wealth kept for its owner's harm refers to קרח's riches.
steps.simpleTranslation: "Wealth kept by its owner, to his harm." ריש לקיש said: This is the wealth of קרח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic, קרח's wealth. ריש לקיש explains a פסוק in קהלת as being about קרח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קרח's great wealth did not help him. It went down into the ground with him. So it is a clear example of riches that hurt their owner.

keyTerms.meaning: The man who led the rebellion against משה

phrases.english: "Wealth kept by its owner to his harm."
phrases.notes: קהלת 5:12

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
This is the wealth of Korach.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the teacher series and opens a new topic about קרח's wealth.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק in קהלת about harmful wealth refers to קרח.

steps.title: A verse shows that קרח had great wealth
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר explains that 'the substance at their feet' means a person's money, which stands him on his feet. This shows קרח was rich.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And all the substance that was at their feet." רבי אלעזר said: This is a person's money, which stands him on his feet.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק to show that קרח really was wealthy, backing up ריש לקיש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק describes what was swallowed with קרח's group. רבי אלעזר reads "at their feet" as money, because money is what keeps a person standing. So קרח lost great riches.

keyTerms.meaning: Stands him on his feet, keeps him going

phrases.english: "And all the substance that was at their feet"
phrases.notes: דברים 11:6. It is about what was swallowed up with קרח's group.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
This is a person's money
which stands him on his feet.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports ריש לקיש's claim by showing from a פסוק that קרח was wealthy.
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברים 11:6, read by רבי אלעזר as referring to money.

steps.title: קרח's keys needed three hundred mules
steps.stepSummary: רבי לוי describes קרח's wealth: just the keys to his storehouses filled 300 white mules, even though they were made of light leather.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי לוי said: The keys to קרח's storehouses were a load for three hundred white mules, and all the keys and locks were made of leather.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי לוי adds a picture of how huge קרח's wealth was.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Leather keys are very light. If even light keys needed 300 mules to carry, the number of storehouses must have been enormous.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Levi said:
A load for three hundred white mules

phrases.aramaic: הָיוּ מַפְתְּחוֹת שֶׁל בֵּית גְּנָזָיו שֶׁל קֹרַח,
phrases.english: were the keys of Korach's storehouses,
and all of the keys and locks were of leather.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי לֵוִי: מַשּׂוֹי שְׁלֹשׁ מֵאוֹת פְּרָדוֹת לְבָנוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a vivid description of how great קרח's wealth was.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קרח's wealth was so great that his leather keys alone needed 300 mules.

steps.title: The three treasures that יוסף hid in Egypt
steps.stepSummary: רבי חמא ברבי חנינא says יוסף hid three treasures in מצרים. One was found by קרח, one by אנטונינוס, and one is saved for צדיקים in the future.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חמא ברבי חנינא said: יוסף hid three treasures in מצרים. One was revealed to קרח, one was revealed to אנטונינוס son of אסוירוס, and one is stored away for the צדיקים in the future to come.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains where קרח's huge wealth came from. He found one of יוסף's hidden treasures.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answers the natural question of how קרח became so rich. It came from treasure יוסף stored in מצרים. The third treasure is still hidden, waiting for the צדיקים.

keyTerms.meaning: A Roman ruler known from the גמרא

steps.whatToRemember: קרח had enormous wealth from one of יוסף's hidden treasures. It did not help him at all; it was "wealth kept to his harm."

phrases.english: Rabbi Chama son of Rabbi Chanina said:
Yosef hid three treasures in Egypt.
One was revealed to Korach,
and one was revealed to Antoninus son of Asverus,
and one is stored away for the righteous in the future to come.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חָמָא בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא: שָׁלֹשׁ מַטְמוֹנִיּוֹת הִטְמִין יוֹסֵף בְּמִצְרַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the source of the great wealth described in the previous steps.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קרח's wealth came from one of three treasures יוסף hid in מצרים.

steps.title: קרח was neither swallowed nor burned
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says קרח was not among those swallowed by the earth and not among those burned by fire. He proves both points from the exact wording of the פסוקים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: קרח was not swallowed and not burned. The פסוק about the swallowing says "all the men who belonged to קרח," which means his people but not קרח himself. The פסוק about the fire says "two hundred and fifty men," which also leaves out קרח.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן makes a new statement about קרח's death. He reads two פסוקים carefully to show that קרח himself was in neither group.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each פסוק names a group, and רבי יוחנן reads what is left out. "The men who belonged to קרח" means his followers, not קרח himself. "Two hundred and fifty men" were the incense offerers, and that count does not include קרח.

keyTerms.meaning: those who were swallowed by the earth
those who were burned by the fire
but not קרח himself (a reading of what the פסוק leaves out)

steps.confusionAlert: There were two punishments in קרח's rebellion. The earth swallowed one group, and fire burned the 250 men offering incense. Keep the two groups separate in your mind.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
Korach was not among the swallowed
and not among the burned.
Not among the swallowed, as it is written:
"and all the men who belonged to Korach"
phrases.notes: במדבר 16:32

phrases.english: but not Korach himself.
And not among the burned, as it is written:
"when the fire consumed two hundred and fifty men"
phrases.notes: במדבר 26:10

phrases.english: but not Korach.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: קֹרַח לֹא מִן הַבְּלוּעִים וְלֹא מִן הַשְּׂרוּפִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of statements about קרח, moving from his wealth to his death.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קרח was neither swallowed nor burned, based on how each פסוק names its group without him.

steps.title: A ברייתא says קרח was both swallowed and burned
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא takes the opposite view. It says קרח was both swallowed and burned, and brings other פסוקים to show it.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: קרח was among both the burned and the swallowed. He was swallowed, as it says "it swallowed them and קרח." He was burned, as it says "fire came out from ה׳ and consumed the two hundred and fifty men," and קרח was with them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that disagrees with רבי יוחנן. According to it, קרח suffered both punishments.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא uses a different swallowing פסוק, one that names קרח directly. For the burning, it says קרח was together with the 250 men, so the fire took him too. The גמרא does not decide between the two views.

keyTerms.meaning: it was taught in a ברייתא (a teaching from the time of the משנה)

phrases.english: It was taught in a baraita:
Korach was among the burned and among the swallowed.
Among the swallowed, as it is written:
"and it swallowed them and Korach."
phrases.notes: במדבר 26:10. This פסוק names קרח himself.

phrases.english: Among the burned, as it is written:
"And fire went out from before ה׳
[And fire came forth from ה׳]
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets match how the פסוק actually reads.

phrases.english: and consumed the two hundred and fifty men,"
phrases.notes: במדבר 16:35

phrases.english: and Korach was with them.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַתְנִיתָא תָּנָא: קֹרַח מִן הַשְּׂרוּפִין וּמִן הַבְּלוּעִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents a ברייתא with the opposite opinion to רבי יוחנן in step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קרח was both swallowed and burned.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two views. רבי יוחנן says קרח was in neither group. The ברייתא says he was in both.

steps.title: The sun and moon refuse to shine until justice is done for משה
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains a פסוק in חבקוק. During קרח's rebellion, the sun and moon went up to the heaven called זבול and refused to come out unless ה׳ did justice for משה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: What does the פסוק "Sun and moon stood in זבול; by the light of Your arrows they go" mean? It teaches that the sun and moon went up to זבול. They said before ה׳: Master of the World, if You do justice for בן עמרם, we will go out. If not, we will not go out.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא opens a new teaching. He explains a פסוק to show that the sun and moon took a stand for משה's honor during קרח's rebellion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word זבולה tells רבא that the sun and moon went up to a high heaven. Their protest was a refusal to shine until משה was proven right against קרח.

phrases.english: Rava said: What is meant by what is written:
"Sun and moon stood in zevul,
by the light of Your arrows they go"?
phrases.notes: חבקוק 3:11

phrases.english: It teaches that the sun and moon went up to zevul.
They said before Him: Master of the World,

phrases.aramaic: אִם אַתָּה עוֹשֶׂה דִּין לְבֶן עַמְרָם
phrases.english: if You do justice for the son of Amram,
we will go out, and if not, we will not go out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from how קרח died to a new aggadah about the sun and moon protesting for משה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The sun and moon refused to shine until ה׳ did justice for משה.

steps.title: ה׳ shoots arrows at the sun and moon and rebukes them
steps.stepSummary: The sun and moon did not come out until ה׳ shot arrows at them. He scolded them for protesting about a person's honor when they never protested about His. Even today, they only go out after being struck.
steps.simpleTranslation: They did not go out until He shot arrows at them. He said to them: For My honor you did not protest, but for the honor of flesh and blood you protest? And nowadays, they do not go out until they are struck.
steps.whatsHappening: This continues רבא's story. ה׳ answers the sun and moon's protest with arrows and a rebuke, explaining the words "by the light of Your arrows they go."
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rebuke is about priorities. People worship the sun and moon, which insults ה׳'s honor, yet they never protested that. The story ends by explaining why they hesitate to come out each day even now.

keyTerms.meaning: flesh and blood, a human being

phrases.english: Until He shot arrows at them.
phrases.notes: The גמרא leaves out a step here: they did not come out until this happened.

phrases.english: He said to them: For My honor you did not protest,
but for the honor of flesh and blood you protest?
And nowadays they do not go out
until they are struck.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רבא's story from step 24 and explains the second half of the פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ה׳ rebuked the sun and moon for protesting over a person's honor but not over His own. To this day, they come out only when struck.

steps.title: משה asks ה׳ about creating גיהנם
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains משה's words "if ה׳ creates a creation." משה said that if גיהנם was already created, good, and if not, ה׳ should create it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא expounded: What does the פסוק "But if ה׳ creates a creation, and the ground opens its mouth" mean? משה said before the Holy One, Blessed be He: If גיהנם is already created, good. If not, let ה׳ create it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a new explanation of משה's words before the earth swallowed קרח. This sets up the גמרא's question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא splits the doubled words בריאה יברא into two parts. "If it is created" refers to whether גיהנם already exists. "Let ה׳ create" is משה's request if it does not.

phrases.english: Rava expounded: What is meant by what is written:
"But if ה׳ creates a creation,
and the ground opens its mouth"?
phrases.notes: במדבר 16:30

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר מֹשֶׁה לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא:
phrases.english: Moshe said before the Holy One, Blessed be He:
"If it is created," meaning Gehinnom, good,
phrases.notes: רבא reads "if it is a creation" as "if גיהנם was already created."

phrases.english: and if not, "let ה׳ create" it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second teaching of רבא, returning to the swallowing of קרח's group.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: משה asked that if גיהנם did not already exist, ה׳ should create it.

steps.title: What exactly was משה asking for
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what משה meant by "let ה׳ create." It suggests he meant actually creating גיהנם.
steps.simpleTranslation: For what? If you say he meant to actually create it...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question about רבא's explanation. It offers a first guess, which it will challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The simplest reading is that משה wanted גיהנם created right then. The גמרא raises this guess only to test it.

phrases.english: For what?
If you say to actually create it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of משה's request in step 26.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What משה was asking ה׳ to do when he said "let ה׳ create."

steps.title: Nothing is new under the sun
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the guess. A פסוק says nothing is new under the sun, so ה׳ does not make brand-new creations after the creation of the world.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it says: "There is nothing new under the sun"!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the idea that משה asked for גיהנם to be newly created. A פסוק says nothing new is ever made.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If nothing new is created after the six days of creation, משה could not have been asking for a new גיהנם. So the guess from step 27 cannot be right.

keyTerms.meaning: but isn't it so that... (introducing a challenge)
there is nothing new under the sun

phrases.english: But it says: "There is nothing new under the sun"!
phrases.notes: קהלת 1:9

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the guess offered in step 27.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that משה asked for גיהנם to be literally created then.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: קהלת says nothing new comes into being, so a new creation is impossible.

steps.title: משה asked for the opening of גיהנם to be brought close
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that משה was not asking for a new creation. He asked ה׳ to bring the opening of גיהנם close to where קרח's group stood.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he asked to bring its opening close.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the challenge. משה's request was only to move the opening of the already existing גיהנם nearby.
steps.deeperAnalysis: גיהנם already existed, so nothing new was made. The only change was the location of its opening, which let the earth open its mouth right under קרח's group.
steps.whatToRemember: משה did not ask for anything new to be created. He asked for the opening of גיהנם to be brought close, so it fits with "nothing new under the sun."

phrases.english: Rather, to bring the opening close.
phrases.notes: He means the opening of גיהנם, brought right to where קרח's group was standing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 28 by reinterpreting the request from step 27.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: משה asked for גיהנם to be created from scratch.
steps.terutzMaskana: משה asked only for the existing גיהנם's opening to be brought close.

steps.title: The sons of קרח were given a safe place in גיהנם
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains the פסוק 'the sons of קרח did not die': a protected place was set aside for them in גיהנם, where they sat and sang.
steps.simpleTranslation: About the פסוק 'And the sons of קרח did not die,' it was taught in the name of our teacher: a place was set aside and protected for them in גיהנם, and they sat on it and sang songs of praise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that explains a פסוק about קרח's sons. They went down with everyone else but were kept safe in a special spot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the sons of קרח did not die, even though the ground swallowed his group. The ברייתא settles this: they went down, but a protected place was made for them inside גיהנם. Instead of being punished, they sat there and sang.

keyTerms.meaning: Was set apart and protected, like a fortress

phrases.english: "And the sons of Korah did not die."
phrases.notes: במדבר 26:11

phrases.english: It was taught: in the name of our teacher they said:
A place was set apart and protected for them in Gehinnom
and they sat on it and said song.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns to a new פסוק in the קרח story, explaining what happened to קרח's sons when his group was swallowed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The sons of קרח went down but were kept safe in a protected place in גיהנם, where they sang.

steps.title: רבה בר בר חנה is shown the smoking cracks of קרח's group
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה tells how a traveler showed him two smoking cracks where קרח's group was swallowed. A wet piece of wool held over them got singed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said: Once I was walking on the road, and an Arab traveler said to me, 'Come, I will show you where קרח's group was swallowed.' I went and saw two cracks in the ground with smoke coming out. He took a tuft of wool, soaked it in water, put it on the tip of his spear, and passed it over the cracks. It got singed.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר בר חנה tells a story about seeing the place where קרח's group was swallowed. This sets up what he heard there in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story shows that the punishment of קרח's group is still going on. The wool was soaked in water, so it should not burn easily, yet it got singed, which shows how hot it is down there.

keyTerms.meaning: The ones from קרח's group who were swallowed
Cracks or openings in the ground

phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Chana said:
One time I was walking on the road,
a certain Arab traveler said to me:
Come and I will show you the swallowed ones of Korah.
I went and saw two cracks
with smoke coming out of them.
He took a tuft of wool,
soaked it in water,
placed it on the tip of his spear,
and passed it over there. It got singed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה: זִימְנָא חֲדָא הֲוָה קָאָזֵילְנָא בְּאוֹרְחָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After hearing about the sons of קרח who were saved, we now hear about the rest of the group, who are still being punished.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The place where קרח's group was swallowed still gives off smoke and burning heat.

steps.title: The swallowed group admits that משה and his Torah are true
steps.stepSummary: The traveler told רבה בר בר חנה to listen, and he heard voices from below saying: 'משה and his תורה are true, and we are liars.'
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to me, 'Listen, what do you hear?' And I heard them saying this: 'משה and his תורה are true, and they are liars.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is the end of the story: the voices from the ground admit that משה was right. It closes this part of the קרח discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קרח's group had fought against משה and called him a liar. Now, from inside their punishment, they admit the opposite: משה and his תורה are true, and they were the liars.

keyTerms.meaning: Liars, people who make things up

steps.whatToRemember: The sons of קרח were saved in a protected spot where they sang. The rest of קרח's group is still being punished, and they admit that משה and his תורה are true and they were the liars.

phrases.english: He said to me: Listen, what do you hear?
And I heard them saying this:
"Moshe and his Torah are true,
and they are liars."
phrases.notes: "They" means the speakers themselves. They are calling themselves the liars.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רבה בר בר חנה's story by telling what he heard from the cracks.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קרח's swallowed group admits that משה and his תורה are true and that they were the liars.
